title: Committee of Supply – Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)

sections.label: SCDF Türkiye earthquake deployment return
sections.summary: The 68-officer SCDF Operation Lionheart contingent, including two NSmen doctors and four canines, returned after search and rescue deployment in Türkiye following an earthquake killing over 50,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: On 18 February 2023, the Operation Lionheart contingent of the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF), comprising 68 officers, which included two Full-time National Servicemen (NSmen) doctors and four canines, returned home after being deployed in Türkiye for search and rescue operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This followed the devastating earthquake that has, to-date, killed more than 50,000 people in the region.

sections.label: Home Team technology investment questions
sections.summary: A Member asks how much the Home Team has invested in technological solutions in the past five years, while supporting such investment for operational efficiencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Whilst it is correct that we, in the House, support the Home Team's investment in technology to achieve operational efficiencies, we also need to be able to gauge the effectiveness of investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I, therefore, wish to ask the hon Minister the following questions:  How much has the Home Team invested in technological solutions in the past five years?

sections.label: Untracked data and seized virtual assets
sections.summary: The Minister said his Ministry does not track such data, and the Member seeks a review, citing a five-month 2022 seizure of $172.8 million in virtual assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The hon Minister informed that his Ministry does not track such data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I seek a review, as just a few days ago, the hon Minister of State announced in this House, that over a five-month period in 2022, virtual assets amounting to $172.8 million were seized.

sections.label: Recidivism rates and Uplifting Employment Credit
sections.summary: The five-year recidivism rate is 39.9% and the two-year rate rose 0.4% to 20.4%, while Budget 2023's Uplifting Employment Credit incentivises employing desistors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The five-year recidivism rate of 39.9%, which I believe is being released for the first time this year, is an encouraging statistic, even though there is a slight increase in the two-year recidivism rate by 0.4% to 20.4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I was glad to note that the Government has announced in Budget 2023 the Uplifting Employment Credit (UEC) for companies to employ desistors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This was something that I pushed for in this House when I suggested that the Jobs Growth Incentive (JGI) for ex-offenders, to help them during the COVID-19 pandemic, be turned into a permanent scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Government's UEC creates an important incentive for employers to seriously consider investing in our desistors.

sections.label: SPS volunteers and desistor reintegration plans
sections.summary: The Member suggests SPS and its volunteers partner MSF, MND and other agencies to co-create bespoke plans with incentives and disincentives during desistors' supervision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I understand that SPS has, over the years, built a substantial number of volunteers who are roped in to help with reintegration support for prison inmates and desistors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I believe that there is a case for SPS and its volunteers to partner the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), Ministry of National Development (MND) and other Government agencies to co-create bespoke plans for each desistor that has a series of incentives and disincentives during the supervision period of desistors.

sections.label: Desistor permanent employment rate target
sections.summary: The Member asks what the permanent employment rate among desistors is and what realistic stretch target could be achieved in coming years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: What is the permanent employment rate amongst our desistors?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: What would be the realistic stretch target for us to achieve in the years to come?

sections.label: New citizens and fertility rate
sections.summary: New citizens are described as a critical pillar for Singapore's future given a total fertility rate of 1.05.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chairman, new citizens are going to be even more important to the future of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With our total fertility rate at the historical low of 1.05, it will not be hyperbole to say new citizens are a critical pillar in the shape of any future Singapore.

sections.label: English spoken at home
sections.summary: Singapore Census 2020 showed 48.3% of residents spoke English most frequently at home, up from 32.3% ten years earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, the latest Singapore Census 2020 revealed that 48.3% of the resident population in Singapore spoke English most frequently at home, compared to 32.3% a mere 10 years ago.

sections.label: Cyber crime threats and scams
sections.summary: 1.8 million web threats were blocked between April and June 2022, and about $661 million was lost to online scams in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In relation to cyber dependent crimes, a total of 1.8 million web threats against Internet users were detected and blocked in Singapore between April and June 2022, according to data obtained from Kaspersky Security Network, and this was a 17.6% rise from the previous year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: On cyber-enabled crimes, The Straits Times reported that around $661 million was lost to online scams in 2022.

sections.label: Youth radicalisation and ISA orders
sections.summary: Two Singaporean teenagers were issued orders under the Internal Security Act, including a 15-year-old, the youngest dealt with under it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   We have seen more cases of youth radicalisation recently and they are getting younger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Just a few weeks ago, we were shocked with reports of two Singaporean teenagers being issued orders under the Internal Security Act (ISA) for terrorism-related activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One of them, a 15-year-old teenager, is the youngest person to be dealt with under the ISA.

sections.label: Recidivism rates rising
sections.summary: The two-year recidivism rate was 26.1% and the five-year rate 45.2%, both up, with higher long-term chances of re-offending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Both the two-year recidivism rate at 26.1% and the five-year recidivism rate at 45.2%, were up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Separately, the consistently higher five-year rates point to the fact that, over the longer term, the chances of re-offending are higher.

sections.label: Tackling long-term recidivism
sections.summary: The passage states that long-term recidivism rates should be tackled on a five-year period horizon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: While the numbers are good, we cannot rest on our laurels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: We should tackle long-term recidivism rates on a five-year period horizon.

sections.label: Criminal records, halfway houses, Malay drug abusers
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MHA review the Registration of Criminals Act and support women's halfway houses, and notes Malay drug abuser arrests fell 21% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Second, I hope that MHA will consider reviewing the Registration of Criminals Act in the treatment and type of offences that are spent, including the duration of the past offence before a criminal record is spent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Third, taking off my interaction with the community, I suggest that MHA give more support for halfway houses and shelters specially catered for women, including those run by charities, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and religious organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: (In Malay):   The number of new Malay drug abusers arrested has decreased by 21% in 2022, compared to the previous year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: In 2021, the number of Malay drug offenders arrested dropped by 15%; compared to other communities who declined by 7%.

sections.label: Scam losses and cybercrime cases
sections.summary: Scam losses rose from $632 million in 2021 to $660.7 million in 2022, with cases up about 25% to 33,669, mostly victims aged 10 to 49.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Year on year, the total amount reported to have been cheated from all scams rose from $632 million in 2021 to $660.7 million in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The number of scams and cybercrime cases increased by about 25%, from 26,886 in 2021, to 33,669 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: A whopping 79.4% of cases involved individuals from the ages of 10 to 49 years of age.

sections.label: Government support to combat scams
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will augment its support of the Police to work with industry partners to combat scams and protect the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Given the insidious threat of scams and the disproportionate harm it brings to its victims, I hope that the Government will take steps to augment its support of the Police, by legislation or otherwise, to work with industry partners, such as our financial institutions and other stakeholders, in the process to combat scams and protect the community.

sections.label: Anti-Scam Centre setup
sections.summary: The Anti-Scam Centre was set up last year as a collaboration between the Singapore Police Force and six banks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Anti-Scam Centre was set up last year as a collaboration between Singapore Police Force (SPF) and six banks.

sections.label: Online scam losses and cybercrime
sections.summary: Online scam losses were around $632 million in 2021 and $661 million in 2022, with cybercrime cases up about 25% to 33,669, scams being 94%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The amount lost to online scams the last two years has been staggering, around $632 million in 2021 and $661 million in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The total number of cybercrime cases rose by around 25% to 33,669 cases, compared to 26,886 cases the year before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Of these cybercrime cases, scams accounted for 94%.

sections.label: Investment and job scam losses
sections.summary: Investment scams lost about $198.8 million and job scams about $117.4 million, with young adults aged 20 to 39 making up around 53% of victims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The largest amounts lost were to investment scams, about $198.8 million, followed by job scams, which caused around $117.4 million in losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Somewhat surprisingly, at least to me, the largest group of victims were young adults, aged 20 to 39, who made up around 53% of all victims.

sections.label: Young scam and drug arrestees
sections.summary: In 2022, almost 60% of e-commerce scam arrestees were under 29, and cannabis abusers arrested rose 71% to 236, over 60% under 30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For first half of 2022, almost 60% of arrestees for e-commerce scams were aged below 29.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While the drug situation in Singapore remains largely curbed, CNB reported that cannabis abusers arrested in 2022 climbed 71% to 236.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Worryingly, over 60% of arrestees were aged below 30, and some even as young as 14.

sections.label: 2022 scam cases and losses
sections.summary: 2022 saw a record 34,000 cases and a loss of well over S$660 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The year 2022 saw both a record 34,000 cases and a loss of well over S$660 million.

sections.label: Anti-Scam Command bank and telco actions
sections.summary: The Anti-Scam Command partnered with banks to freeze over 16,700 accounts and telcos to terminate over 6,500 lines, preventing about S$146 million in losses in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Anti-Scam Command has also done well, partnering local banks to freeze more than 16,700 bank accounts and telcos to terminate more than 6,500 lines, thereby preventing a further loss of about S$146 million in 2022.

sections.label: Online Criminal Harms Act introduction
sections.summary: MHA will introduce the Online Criminal Harms Act later this year, which first expands the scope of regulatory levers for online criminal activities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: MHA will, therefore, be introducing the Online Criminal Harms Act later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The proposed Online Criminal Harms Act builds on our current laws in three ways.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: First, it will expand the scope of regulatory levers that we can apply to online criminal activities.

sections.label: Upstream measures against scams
sections.summary: The new legislation will introduce upstream measures to detect and reduce scams, such as safeguards against inauthentic accounts.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To Mr Derrick Goh's question on how online entities can be involved in prevention and be held more accountable, the new legislation will introduce upstream measures to detect and reduce scams, such as safeguards against inauthentic accounts.

sections.label: 2022 gambling legislation amendment
sections.summary: In 2022, gambling legislation was amended to keep laws up-to-date and address emerging trends.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In 2022, we amended our gambling legislation to ensure that our laws are up-to-date and able to address emerging trends.

sections.label: Loot boxes class licensing regime
sections.summary: Games with loot boxes are allowed via a class licensing regime if the game fulfils either of two conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: They may feature a range of virtual items of value, which a player may win with varying probabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We allow games with such loot boxes via a class licensing regime, but only if the game fulfils either of two conditions.

sections.label: Home Team capability development spending
sections.summary: Over the past five years, about 30% of the Home Team's expenditure on average went to capability development, including new technological solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Over the past five years, an average of about 30% of the Home Team's expenditure has been on capability development, including investing in new technological solutions.

sections.label: Automated clearance for motorcyclists
sections.summary: Since January 2017, 100% automated clearance has been implemented for all motorcyclists at the land checkpoints.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Since January 2017, we have implemented 100% automated clearance for all motorcyclists at the land checkpoints.

sections.label: Target of 500 positions
sections.summary: The target is to fill a total of 500 positions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The target is to fill a total of 500 positions.

sections.label: Responses to fire and cardiac cases
sections.summary: From 2015 to January this year, they responded to over 3,000 minor fire cases, 6,000 suspected cardiac arrest cases and saved more than 40 lives.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: From 2015 to January this year, they have responded to over 3,000 minor fire cases, 6,000 suspected cardiac arrest cases and saved more than 40 lives.

sections.label: Exercise Northstar XI on Jurong Island
sections.summary: In March this year, the Home Team will conduct Exercise Northstar XI, testing multi-agency responses to a terrorist attack on Jurong Island with over 300 participants.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In March this year, the Home Team will be conducting Exercise Northstar XI, a major ground exercise which will test multi-agency responses to a terrorist attack on Jurong Island.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Exercise Northstar will bring together over 300 participants from agencies, such as SCDF, SPF, Singapore Armed Forces (SAF), JTC and private sector partners.

sections.label: Social integration markers for applicants
sections.summary: It states that markers of social integration considered include family ties to Singaporeans, length of residency, national school study and NS completion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Instead, we consider various markers of social integration, such as family ties to Singaporeans, length of residency, whether the applicant studied in our national schools or completed NS.

sections.label: Online Criminal Harms Act introduction
sections.summary: It states that the online medium is increasingly used for crimes, so MHA will introduce the Online Criminal Harms Act later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We have witnessed the online medium increasingly being used to facilitate crimes, such as large-scale scam operations and malicious cyber activities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Therefore, later this year, MHA will introduce the Online Criminal Harms Act.

sections.label: Benefit to HDB households
sections.summary: It states that when fully implemented over five years, this will benefit 1.1 million HDB households.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: When fully implemented over five years, this will benefit 1.1 million HDB households.

sections.label: Youth ISA terrorism cases
sections.summary: It states ISA figures for youths aged 20 and below from 2002 to 2014 and since 2015, and ISD outreach events in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: From 2002 to 2014, only two youths aged 20 were dealt with under the ISA for terrorism-related activities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Since 2015, ISA orders were issued to 11 self-radicalised youths aged 20 and below.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In 2022, ISD organised close to 70 counter-terrorism or radicalisation outreach events in schools and Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) targeting students and educators.

sections.label: School PDE engagements in 2023
sections.summary: It states that secondary schools which did not do a PDE engagement in the last two years will conduct at least one in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Secondary schools which did not do a PDE engagement in the last two years, will conduct at least one engagement in 2023.

sections.label: Bill amending Misuse of Drugs Act
sections.summary: It states that on 24 February MHA introduced a Bill to amend the Misuse of Drugs Act to control psychoactive substances by psychoactive effects.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: On 24 February, MHA introduced a Bill to amend the Misuse of Drugs Act to control psychoactive substances based on their capacity to produce psychoactive effects rather than their chemical structure alone.

sections.label: CoSS rollout to supervisees
sections.summary: CoSS will be progressively rolled out to all supervisees by June this year, following good pilot results.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As the pilot has shown good results, I am pleased to announce that CoSS will be progressively rolled out to all supervisees by June this year.

sections.label: Singapore recidivism rates
sections.summary: Singapore's two-year recidivism rate is low and stable at around 20% for the 2020 release cohort, while the five-year rate is between 40% and 43%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Singapore's two-year recidivism rate is low and stable at around 20% for the 2020 release cohort.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Our five-year rate is higher, at between 40% and 43%.

sections.label: Inmate training programme completion
sections.summary: As of 2022, 422 inmates completed training programmes, and in 2023 YRSG will expand TAP & Grow to Food Services, expected to benefit up to 700 inmates and ex-offenders annually.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As of 2022, a total of 422 inmates have completed the training programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In 2023, YRSG will expand TAP & Grow to Food Services, which we expect to benefit up to 700 inmates and ex-offenders annually.

sections.label: Yellow Ribbon Community Project engagement
sections.summary: YRCP grassroots volunteers have engaged over 19,000 families since 2010, linking them to community assistance and ensuring their well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Yellow Ribbon Community Project (YRCP) grassroots volunteers have engaged over 19,000 families since 2010, linking them to community assistance and ensuring their well-being.

sections.label: Rise Above Halfway House
sections.summary: In September 2022, SPS set up a secular all-women halfway house named Rise Above Halfway House, and as of February 2023, 31 female offenders have been emplaced there.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In September 2022, SPS set up a secular all-women halfway house, named Rise Above Halfway House (RAHWH).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As of February 2023, 31 female offenders have been emplaced to RAHWH.

sections.label: FITRAH mosque support
sections.summary: FITRAH has galvanised all 71 mosques to support inmates, ex-offenders and their family, beyond zakat assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: FITRAH has galvanised all 71 mosques to support inmates, ex-offenders and their family, beyond zakat assistance.

sections.label: MMO Rehabilitation Network launch
sections.summary: The MMO Rehabilitation Network was launched in November 2021, bringing together 26 MMOs and all eleven M³@Towns.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In November 2021, we launched the MMO Rehabilitation Network, which brings together 26 MMOs and all eleven M³@Towns.

sections.label: 2022 scam cases and losses
sections.summary: In 2022, 31,728 scam cases were seen, a 32.6% increase from 2021, with over $660 million lost, 4.5% higher than 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In 2022, we saw 31,728 scam cases, a 32.6% increase from 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: More than $660 million was lost, 4.5% higher than 2021.

sections.label: Anti-scam enforcement operations 2022
sections.summary: In 2022, 25 islandwide anti-scam enforcement operations led to over 8,000 money mules and scammers being investigated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In 2022, 25 islandwide anti-scam enforcement operations led to over 8,000 money mules and scammers being investigated.

sections.label: CDSA and Penal Code amendments
sections.summary: MHA will amend the CDSA to prescribe specific conduct for holding mules criminally liable, and is working with SNDGO on Penal Code amendments to curb Singpass abuse.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Based on current laws, we need to prove that the money mule knew that the monies he was handling were linked to criminal activity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will amend the Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act, or CDSA, to prescribe specific conduct for which we can hold mules criminally liable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: MHA is also working with SNDGO on legislative amendments to the Penal Code to curb abuse of Singpass credentials as a vector to perpetrate scams.

sections.label: National anti-scam campaign ACT
sections.summary: A national anti-scam campaign with the tagline "I can ACT against scams" was launched in January, and a Scam Public Education Office will launch later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In January this year, we launched a new national anti-scam campaign with the tagline "I can ACT against scams" as our rallying call.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: ACT is an acronym for three key actions that each of us can take to keep ourselves safe from scams. "A" stands for Adding security features, such as installing the ScamShield app on mobile devices. "C" stands for Checking for scam signs and verifying with official sources. "T" stands for Telling authorities, family and friends about scams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will be launching the Scam Public Education Office later this year to drive our collective efforts with community partners and expand our outreach on scams, including (a) collaborating with National Crime Prevention Council (NCPC) to create and curate anti-scam public education content at the national level; and (b) working with private sector and community agencies to tailor our anti-scam public education efforts for different population segments.

sections.label: ScamShield 2.0 WhatsApp chatbot
sections.summary: ScamShield allows users to report scam calls and SMSes, and MHA is working with GovTech to roll out ScamShield 2.0 with a WhatsApp chatbot.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: It also allows users to report scam calls and scam SMSes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We are working closely with GovTech to roll out ScamShield 2.0, which will include a WhatsApp chatbot for the public to report scam messages.

sections.label: INTERPOL asset seizure statistic
sections.summary: The $172.8 million asset seizure was a statistic from an INTERPOL article about a global operation Singapore joined.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The seizure of $172.8 million in assets that Mr Pillai referred to, was a statistic quoted from INTERPOL's article, about a global INTERPOL operation that Singapore participated in.

sections.label: Security tenders and officer shifts
sections.summary: New tenders specify outcomes rather than fixed headcount or shift hours, letting agencies decide shift duration and improve conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: New tenders are generally required to specify outcomes, rather than dictate a fixed headcount or shift hours.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This allows security agencies to optimise security solutions that integrate manpower, technology and processes, giving them the flexibility to decide on the duration of each security officer's shift.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Government will continue working with tripartite partners to further improve the working conditions of security officers.

sections.label: Scam victims' non-financial harm
sections.summary: Scam victims often suffer emotional and mental harm beyond financial loss.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Scammed victims are often hurt more than just financially.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: They also suffer emotionally as well as mentally.

sections.label: Census place-of-birth data
sections.summary: Census information on place of birth of PRs and citizens is provided at 10-year intervals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: My point is, based on the latest Census, and the Census before that, in 10-year intervals, information on the place of birth of PRs and citizens are actually provided in 10-yearly intervals.

sections.label: English criterion for citizenship
sections.summary: The member asks whether English is part of assessing individuals for citizenship, saying the Minister did not address it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The second question has to do with my point in the cut, I do not believe Minister addressed it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: It has to do with English as a criterion for citizenship selection because of its utility as a language for better integration between Singaporeans and new citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Can the Minister confirm whether this is part of the process in assessing individuals for citizenship?

sections.label: English test for residency citizenship
sections.summary: The question asks the Leader of the Opposition whether he advocates an English test before permanent residency and citizenship consideration.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: On the second question that he asked for a clarification on, Mdm Chair, if I may ask the Leader of the Opposition: is he advocating that a test of English should be applied before someone can be considered for permanent residency and citizenship?

sections.label: Birthplace data and English test
sections.summary: Speaker argues birthplace data is already in the 10-year Census and questions using an English test for new citizens and PRs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Just on the first clarification that Minister provided, I do not think Minister answered the question.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I am suggesting that those countries, the information which shows where someone was born is actually already provided in 10-year Census.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I think we have said this on previous occasions.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I think you can imagine the scenario if you publish this information on such a current basis, how this information can be misinterpreted and can also be used to suggest that we are friendly or not as friendly to certain nationalities, and even to certain ethnicities.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: On Mr Singh's advocacy of us using English, perhaps, as a test of the ability of a new citizen or PR to integrate, I must admit to being quite surprised by his position, the reason being that, firstly, one can imagine that for most applicants to permanent residency and citizenship if they have been in Singapore for a number of years, particularly if they had worked here, a facility with English is not surprising.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For those who perhaps do not have the facility with English and/or cannot communicate easily in English, I think from our ground interactions, it is also quite clear who these individuals are likely to be.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: They are likely to be spouses of citizens or other PRs and have come from the same country of origin and unless we are saying that we, therefore, do not welcome such foreign spouses, then I am not sure to what extent a test of English that could be applied to prevent them from being considered would be helpful.

sections.label: Two people's monetary losses
sections.summary: One person had lost $280,000 and one had lost $80,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: One had lost $280,000 and one having lost $80,000.

sections.label: Proposed kill switch for transfers
sections.summary: Speaker suggests a kill switch to stop money flowing from one account to another before leaving Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: My humble and respectful suggestion is that we build in a "kill switch" that would just stop the flow of money from one account to the next account, prior to it leaving our shores.

sections.label: Existing kill switch and money mules
sections.summary: An emergency self-service kill switch lets customers suspend accounts, but it has not stopped transfers to other accounts, so action against money mules is planned.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Indeed, we have a "kill switch", which I had mentioned in my main reply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: This emergency self-service "kill switch" allows customers to suspend their accounts quickly, if compromised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, while the bank account of the original bank account holder – the victim – has activated the "kill switch" for his or her own account, it has not stopped the monies from being transferred to other accounts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: And that is why what we intend to do with the money mules is an important step, because we want to prevent these money mules from setting up or using multiple bank accounts to allow the scam proceeds to filter through the system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We have also co-located the seven major retail banks together at Anti-Scam Command, so that they can coordinate their efforts.

sections.label: California cannabis emergency visits
sections.summary: In California, after the retail cannabis market opened, emergency visits and admissions related to cannabis use rose 56% from 2016 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For example, in California, after the opening of the retail sales market for cannabis, emergency visits and admissions related to any cannabis use increased by 56% from 2016 to 2019.

sections.label: HTX technology human talent
sections.summary: Developing technologies needs human talent, and HTX intends to fill about 500 positions this year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Even in the way we develop the technologies, we need human talent.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I mentioned in my speech earlier that HTX intends to fill something like 500 positions for this year alone.

sections.label: Retail banks standby services
sections.summary: Seven major retail banks and the SPF provide 24/7 standby services and aim to freeze accounts within an hour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The seven major retail banks are working closely together, together with the SPF, to provide standby services 24/7 and they aim to freeze accounts within an hour.

sections.label: Overseas scam origin, enforcement challenges
sections.summary: Over 90% of known scam cases originated overseas, and working with foreign law enforcement faces many operational challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Based on the numbers I have, more than 90% of scam cases that we know of originated from overseas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Like I have mentioned in my main reply, we work closely with foreign law enforcement agencies, but there are many operational challenges.

sections.label: Recovering scam proceeds, many claimants
sections.summary: Foreign law enforcement cooperation faces operational challenges, and recovered scam proceeds have many claimants, making full return to victims difficult.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Or they may even have been changed into non-cash proceeds, for instance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, I would just like to share with the Member that we definitely work with foreign law enforcement agencies, but we have to be mindful that there are operational challenges, and that even when they are able to recover some portion of the scam proceeds, there are actually many, many claimants to those scam proceeds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: And so, there is some difficulty to be able to return those monies in its totality to the victim.
